name: Non-specific Low Back Pain
summary: Non-specific low back pain (NSLBP) means pain in the lower back, with or without leg pain above the knee, where no specific cause such as fracture, tumour, infection or nerve compression can be identified. Most back pain seen in clinics is in this group.

looksLike: Pain across the lower back, often worse with certain movements or positions, eased by others.
May spread to the buttock or thigh but not with a clear nerve-root pattern.
No progressive weakness, no saddle numbness, no bladder or bowel change.
Pain often changes day to day and is influenced by activity, sleep and stress.
redFlags: Saddle numbness or tingling, new bladder or bowel dysfunction, new sexual dysfunction
Bilateral leg pain or weakness with progression
Major trauma, or minor trauma with older age, osteoporosis or long-term steroid use
Fever, recent infection, intravenous drug use, immune suppression with back pain
Past cancer, unexplained weight loss, age over 50 with new constant pain, night pain
Sudden severe back or abdominal pain with a pulsatile abdominal feeling, older patient
firstSteps: Initial approach: education, reassurance and staying active.
Justifying findings: mechanical pattern, no flags, no nerve signs.
Priority: exercise and function over passive treatment.

assess: Observe posture and gait (with consent and appropriate exposure).
Active movement: flexion, extension, side-bend, rotation. Note range, pain and movement quality.
Repeated movements if pain is mechanical (see E1).
Neurological screen: myotomes L2 to S1, dermatomes, patellar and Achilles reflexes, straight leg raise.
Palpation of spine and muscles; examine hips and sacroiliac joints to exclude mimics.
Functional tasks: sit to stand, squat, lifting, whatever the patient listed as their goal.

tests.name: Repeated movement testing (McKenzie / MDT)
tests.purpose: Find out whether repeated movement in one direction changes symptoms in a lasting and useful way (directional preference)
tests.positive: Pain moves from the leg or buttock toward the centre of the back (centralisation), or pain decreases and range increases and the improvement lasts after the movement

tests.name: Prone instability test
tests.purpose: Check whether pain eased by muscle activation suggests a movement-control problem
tests.positive: Pain present at rest but reduced or gone when the muscles are active

differentials: Visceral causes (kidney stone, aortic aneurysm, pancreatitis)
measures: Record pain (0 to 10), the Oswestry Disability Index or Roland-Morris questionnaire, the patient-specific functional goal, range of movement, walking tolerance and sleep.

tests.name: Repeated movement testing (McKenzie / MDT)
tests.purpose: Find out whether repeated movement in one direction changes symptoms in a lasting and useful way (directional preference)
tests.positive: Pain moves from the leg or buttock toward the centre of the back (centralisation), or pain decreases and range increases and the improvement lasts after the movement
procedure: Ask the patient to do 10 repetitions of one movement, for example prone press-ups (lying on the stomach, pushing the upper body up with the arms). Record pain location before, during and after
tests.interpretation: A direction of movement that may suit exercise treatment If a direction helps, use it as a home exercise. If symptoms peripheralise (spread away from the spine) stop that direction

tests.name: Prone instability test
tests.purpose: Check whether pain eased by muscle activation suggests a movement-control problem
tests.positive: Pain present at rest but reduced or gone when the muscles are active
tests.patientPosition: Prone with the trunk on the bench and feet on the floor
procedure: Step 1: apply posterior-to-anterior pressure over each lumbar segment and note pain. Step 2: ask the patient to lift the feet off the floor to activate the back muscles, and repeat the pressure
tests.interpretation: May suggest a benefit from motor control exercise. Not proof of instability

blocks.text: **Non-specific low back pain (NSLBP)** means pain in the lower back, with or without leg pain above the knee, where no specific cause such as fracture, tumour, infection or nerve compression can be identified. Most back pain seen in clinics is in this group [Ref - to verify].

**Important idea:** non-specific does not mean not real. Pain is real. It means that the examination cannot point to one damaged structure. Pain comes from a mix of tissue sensitivity, movement, load, sleep, mood, beliefs and work factors. This is called a biopsychosocial view [Ref - to verify].
Scan findings such as disc bulges or degeneration are common in people without back pain, so they do not always explain symptoms [Ref - to verify].

items: Pain across the lower back, often worse with certain movements or positions, eased by others.

No progressive weakness, no saddle numbness, no bladder or bowel change.
Pain often changes day to day and is influenced by activity, sleep and stress.

blocks.text: Many episodes improve over weeks, but recurrence is common [Ref - to verify]. This is useful information to share with the patient.

blocks.text: Honest note: most tests for NSLBP have limited ability to identify a specific structure. They guide treatment choice and monitor response. They do not name a damaged tissue.

blocks.text: E3. Straight leg raise (screening only here)
Used to screen for nerve involvement. Full procedure is in Ch 2. A negative screen supports NSLBP. A positive screen moves the patient to the radiculopathy pathway.

sections.title: G. RED FLAGS AND URGENT CONDITIONS

rows: Saddle numbness or tingling, new bladder or bowel dysfunction, new sexual dysfunction
Compression of the lower nerve roots
Stop; same-day hospital emergency referral. Do not wait to see if it improves
Bilateral leg pain or weakness with progression
Major trauma, or minor trauma with older age, osteoporosis or long-term steroid use
Do not load; refer for imaging
Fever, recent infection, intravenous drug use, immune suppression with back pain
Past cancer, unexplained weight loss, age over 50 with new constant pain, night pain
Sudden severe back or abdominal pain with a pulsatile abdominal feeling, older patient

blocks.text: A single red flag does not confirm disease. Many red flags have low accuracy on their own and clusters matter more [Ref - to verify].
**Defer:** manipulation, strong loading and heavy exercise until serious pathology is excluded.

sections.title: H. Working diagnosis and decision pathway

items: Any emergency flag? **Yes:** emergency action.
Any urgent flag? **Yes:** defer treatment and refer.
Leg pain below the knee with root signs? **Yes:** go to Ch 2.

Mechanical back pain, no nerve signs, no flags? **Yes:** working diagnosis is non-specific low back pain. Stratify risk (for example with the STarT Back Screening Tool [Ref - to verify]) to decide how much support is needed.
No flags but unusually high disability or distress? Add psychosocial strategies and consider combined care.

rows: Graded mobilization of lumbar or thoracic spine
May give short-term pain relief and make movement easier [Ref - to verify]
Stiff painful segment, patient prefers hands-on
Prone, central or unilateral postero-anterior glides, low to moderate grade, 30 to 60 seconds per segment
Leg symptoms spread; increased pain after treatment
Option for short-term relief in some patients [Ref - to verify]
No red flags, no nerve compromise, patient consents

blocks.text: **Preferred starting choice:** education and active movement first. Manual therapy is an optional adjunct used mainly for short-term relief. Do not claim that it realigns the spine or fixes a disc.

**Is it working?** Look for greater range, easier function and the patient's own rating of change over the same session and the next session. If no benefit after a few sessions, stop and choose another approach.

sections.title: J. Exercise prescription (example starting plan, not universal)

rows: Can increase time without lasting flare
Pain flares for more than a day
Lying on the back with knees bent, rock the pelvis
On hands and knees, round then arch gently
On hands and knees, extend opposite arm and leg
10 reps, a few times a day

blocks.text: **Symptom rule:** discomfort during exercise that settles within a short time is acceptable. Pain spreading into the leg, new numbness or weakness means stop and reassess. This is an example, not a protocol. Different exercise types (strengthening, motor control, aerobic, mixed) seem to help to a similar degree [Ref - to verify], so choose according to patient preference, tolerance and goals.

rows: Not routinely recommended in several guidelines [Ref - to verify]
May be used for comfort if the patient likes it

blocks.text: **Case:** A 38-year-old delivery driver has 3 weeks of central low back pain after lifting boxes. Pain is worse bending forward and sitting long, easier walking. No leg symptoms, normal reflexes, negative SLR, no red flags. Prone press-ups reduce his pain and it stays reduced afterwards. He worries that his back is damaged.

**Working diagnosis:** non-specific mechanical low back pain with a possible extension directional preference. **Plan:** explain the favourable outlook, press-ups several times a day, walking, short driving breaks, progressive lifting practice, reassess in a week.
**Questions and answers**

items: Why is a scan not needed here? Imaging rarely changes management in flag-free back pain, and many scan findings also occur in people without symptoms [Ref - to verify].
Why discuss his fear? Fear of damage can lead to avoiding movement, which may prolong disability [Ref - to verify].
What would make you change the plan today? Saddle numbness, bladder change, leg weakness or spreading leg pain. Any of these means stop and use the Section G or Ch 2 pathway.
The press-ups make leg pain worse after 10 repetitions. What next? Stop that direction because symptoms are peripheralising, then test another movement or manage via Ch 2.
Why is TENS not chosen as the main treatment? Evidence shows little added benefit for most patients and it does not address movement or function.
**Initial approach:** education, reassurance and staying active.
**Justifying findings:** mechanical pattern, no flags, no nerve signs.
**Priority:** exercise and function over passive treatment.
**Manual therapy:** optional short-term adjunct.
**Exercise:** walking, mobility, trunk and hip strengthening, directional preference if found.
**Modalities:** not routine.
**Tell the patient:** most people improve; movement is safe; flare-ups are usual and manageable.
**Avoid:** bed rest, fear-based messages, unnecessary scans, long-term bracing.
**Measure:** pain, disability questionnaire, goal task.
**If no improvement:** review diagnosis and psychosocial factors; consider other care.
**Referral triggers:** Section G.
**Discharge:** goals met and self-management understood.
**Can be tested:** whether exercise and education improve pain and function; whether subgroup strategies (e.g. STarT Back) improve outcomes.
**Hypotheses:** that a directional preference identifies a mechanism; that motor control exercise works by restoring control.
**Future questions:** which patients benefit most from which exercise type; how to prevent recurrence.

sections.A: Non-specific kamar dard woh dard hai jis ki koi khaas wajah (fracture, tumour, infection ya nerve root) nahi milti. Yeh sab se aam kamar dard hai aur aksar theek ho jata hai.
sections.B: Kamar ke neeche dard jo kuch movements ya positions se barhta aur kuch se kam hota hai. Kooleh ya ran tak ja sakta hai, lekin nerve ke pattern mein ghutne se neeche nahi.
sections.C: Kab aur kaise shuru hua, kya barhata aur kya kam karta hai, raat ko jagata hai ya nahi, aur red flags: yeh sawaal mechanical aur serious dard ka farq batate hain.
sections.D: Posture aur chaal, kamar ki movements, baar baar movement ka asar (repeated movements), aur neuro screen.
sections.E: Yeh tests koi khaas tuuti hui cheez nahi batate. Yeh treatment chunne aur behtari check karne mein madad karte hain.
sections.F: Sciatica (ghutne se neeche nerve pattern), spinal stenosis aur doosri conditions ka farq table mein hai.
sections.G: Saddle area mein sunn-pan, peshab ya pakhane ki nayi tabdeeli, dono taangon mein barhti kamzori: yeh cauda equina ka khatra hai, foran emergency.
sections.H: Pehle emergency flags, phir urgent flags, phir ghutne se neeche nerve signs (Chapter 2). Kuch na ho aur dard mechanical ho to non-specific kamar dard.
sections.I: Halki mobilisation aur soft tissue kaam se thori der ka aaraam milta hai. Asal ilaaj exercise aur active rehna hai.
sections.J: Walking, pelvic tilts, cat-camel, bridge, bird-dog aur dheere dheere taaqat barhana.
sections.K: Garmi aaraam ke liye. TENS, ultrasound aur traction aam taur par recommend nahi.
sections.L: Pehli visit: flags screen karein, samjhayein ke serious wajah ka imkaan kam hai, aur active rehne ki salah dein. Phir exercise barhayein aur kaam par wapsi.
sections.M: Dard, ODI ya Roland-Morris, patient ka goal, movement aur chalne ki salahiyat dobara napein.
sections.N: 38 saal ke delivery driver ko boxes uthane ke baad kamar dard hai. Pehle khud plan socho, phir jawab dekho.
sections.chapter-summary-treatment-decision: Mukhtasar: samjhana, tasalli aur active rehna sab se pehle; exercise asal ilaaj hai.
